case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Cabinet for Health & Family Services v. Todd County Standard, Inc.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed enforcement of an unappealed Attorney General open-records decision requiring the Cabinet to produce records about a child who died under circumstances suggesting abuse, held that statutory authority for a record's creation raises a rebuttable presumption that it exists, and upheld the finding that the Cabinet's denial was willful.
key_cases.relevance: The Cabinet's internal fatality review is the state-level review whose outputs are at stake in any public fatality-review effort.
key_cases.quote: The Cabinet cannot benefit from intentionally frustrating the Attorney General's review of an open records request

key_cases.case_name: Cabinet for Health & Family Services v. Courier-Journal, Inc.
key_cases.holding: The court held the production issue moot because the 140 child-fatality and near-fatality case files had already been released, and affirmed the finding that the Cabinet willfully withheld them, upholding roughly $300,000 in attorneys' fees and costs and $756,000 in statutory penalties calculated on a per-record, per-day basis under KRS 61.882(5).
key_cases.relevance: The internal fatality and near-fatality reviews at issue are the raw material of state fatality-review analysis.
key_cases.quote: Public entities must permit inspection of public records as required or risk meaningful punishment for noncompliance
